name: City of Hamilton
tagline: The whole business of Bermuda on one street
description: Bermuda's capital and the base of its insurance and reinsurance industry, built along Front Street facing the harbour with the pastel commercial buildings behind it. It is small enough to cross in fifteen minutes and contains almost everything the island does for work.
bestFor: Anyone working in or with the island's financial sector
pros: The entire professional network within walking distance
Ferries and buses radiate from here
Restaurants and bars on Front Street
cons: The most expensive rents on the island
No beach in the city itself

name: Paget
tagline: Across the harbour, with Elbow Beach
description: The parish directly south of Hamilton across the harbour, holding Elbow Beach, the Botanical Gardens and a good deal of the island's more comfortable housing. The ferry to Hamilton takes minutes and is faster than the road, which is what makes this the practical commute.
bestFor: Anyone working in Hamilton who wants a beach and a ferry
pros: Elbow Beach and the Botanical Gardens
Quieter than the city with the same access
cons: Ferry schedules thin in the evening

name: Warwick
tagline: The south shore beaches and the Railway Trail
description: The parish along the south shore holding Warwick Long Bay and a string of smaller coves with the pink sand Bermuda is known for, and a well-used stretch of the Railway Trail running through it on the old rail bed. Quieter and slightly cheaper than Paget.
bestFor: Anyone whose priority is being able to walk to the south shore beaches
pros: The best stretch of south shore beaches
Railway Trail for walking and cycling

name: St George's
tagline: The oldest English town in the New World
description: The UNESCO-listed town at the eastern end of the island, founded in 1612 and the oldest continuously inhabited English settlement in the Americas, with narrow lanes, St Peter's Church and Tobacco Bay nearby. It is a genuine town rather than a preserved one.
bestFor: Anyone who wants history and quiet more than a Hamilton commute
pros: Tobacco Bay and the east end beaches
cons: Forty-five minutes from Hamilton by bus

name: Royal Naval Dockyard and Sandys
tagline: The west end, the fortress and the ferry
description: The far western tip, built around the Royal Navy's nineteenth-century dockyard, now holding the National Museum, a cruise terminal and the ferry that runs the length of the island to Hamilton in twenty minutes. Sandys parish behind it is residential and green.
bestFor: Anyone who will use the fast ferry and wants to be away from the city
pros: The National Museum and the dockyard fortifications
Somerset Long Bay and the west end beaches
cons: Cruise crowds when ships are in
Ferry is the only quick route
